From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Draft attached (MAP_AthenaPilot_v1.2.xlsx) and a short acceptance-tests-harness doc that enumerates the automated checks we recommend. High-level summary below so your team can scan quickly.

Summary of proposed Acceptance Benchmarks (pilot baseline):
- Functional correctness: >= 92% intent-match on the clinical routing test set (1,200 seed prompts)
- Latency: P95 generation < 300ms for 512-token requests during canary traffic (region: us-west)
- Throughput: sustained 200 reqs/min per dedicated instance without queueing > 250ms
- Stability: < 1% error rate (5000 sample requests across full test matrix)

Exit gates (hard):
1) Failure to hit Functional correctness threshold after two remediation cycles (data + prompt tuning)
2) Sustained P95 latency > 450ms under canary load for 24 hours
3) Error rate > 3% for 6+ hours during smoke regression tests

Exit gates (soft / require review):
- 5–10% dip in intent-match vs baseline (requires ops remediation and re-test)
- Single-day latency spike where downstream SLA still met after retry fallback

Acceptance tests (what we run together):
- Smoke suite: 50 representative live queries across integration points (run daily during pilot)
- Regression harness: 1,200 seed prompts (nightly) comparing outputs against baseline golden set
- End-to-end flow: 3 scripted clinical workflows with telemetry verification (workflows: intake triage, benefits lookup, referral routing)
- Load window: 4-hour 75th percentile run at projected peak load to validate autoscaling policies

Canary sizing recommendation: start with 1000 requests/day routed over 4 hours (peak spread) and scale to 5k/day for the final week of pilot. The attached risk-matrix outlines rollback triggers and owner assignments.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached MAP and acceptance harness and flag edits by Thursday (May 27).
2) We'll run an initial smoke pass with your sandbox on Monday (May 31).
3) If smoke passes, flip canary to 1k/day on Jun 2 and run the 4-week validation window.

I'll also add Ben to help with SLA tuning and the test harness.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_AthenaPilot_v1.2.xlsx, acceptance-tests-harness.md, risk-matrix.pdf

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:41:00 -0700

Sarah — quick operational clarifications from my side:

1) Remediation cycles: we expect two fix windows (each 72 hours) where we can tune prompts/encoders and retest. If the functional correctness threshold isn't met after the second cycle, we'll recommend either extended pilot with scoped fixes or halt (hard exit).

2) Evidence & artifacts for signoff: we will deliver nightly regression reports (CSV + summary), a conformance checklist for each workflow, and the raw logs (redacted) needed for audit. Those are referenced in the attached acceptance-tests-harness.md.

3) Compliance check: your team asked about data residency for logs — for the pilot we propose masking PII and storing logs in US-only buckets; for Private deployment we can arrange VPC-only logging.

4) Risk tolerances: see the risk-matrix.pdf but key callouts are a) fallback to lightweight reranking model if latency spikes, b) manual rollback policy and owner (Ben) for any non-trivial incident.

If this looks good to you, Marcus and I will update the MAP to include your procurement milestones (PO, SOC2 evidence review, contract signature).

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
